A leave one dataset out protocol across five datasets removes partition randomness and exposes domain instability hidden by single dataset checks, giving steadier, more interpretable results.
arxiv-2604-02262: Lehmann derives lineshapes for optical optical double resonance spectra at arbitrary pump and probe strengths from steady state three level density matrix solutions. Without Doppler broadening the probe spectrum is a pair of Lorentzian lines with Autler Townes splitting, each width set by equal relaxation rates. With Doppler broadening, numerical integration is needed except at weak fields. At large Doppler width the lines stay Lorentzian with power broadening, but the width differs for co and counter propagating beams and is largely inhomogeneous.
arxiv-2604-02362: Madishetty presents CIPHER, a dual pathway model that decodes phonemes from high density scalp EEG. It combines event related potential features with broadband coefficients. On binary articulatory tasks it nears ceiling performance, but those tasks prove highly confound vulnerable, with acoustic onset and TMS blocking effects. On the primary 11 class phoneme task with held out subjects, fine grained discrimination proves limited. The author therefore frames the work as a benchmark and feature comparison study, not an EEG to text system.
arxiv-2604-02462: Bell and McNabb explore remote temperature sensing in 2D: gauging steady state heat at one point from high order heat data at another point. The problem connects to the Bergman kernel of the domain, Runge theorem, and near null quadrature identities. The short note links a real gauging question to kernel theory and approx theory.
arxiv-2604-02562: So and Song study four-dimensional toric orbifolds with no odd-degree cohomology. They build an integral basis for the degree-two equivariant cohomology of such a space by taking an intersection of lattices. The build gives a new route to the algebraic cellular basis for integral ordinary cohomology. When the orbifold is an algebraic variety, they also pin down its Cartier divisor group and its Picard group. The result is a concrete basis, not just an existence claim.
arxiv-2604-02662: Yukalov clears up long-standing confusions in the theory of Bose-Einstein condensation. That is the state in which many bosons share one quantum state. He explains that global gauge symmetry breaking is both necessary and sufficient for a condensate. He adds that there is no grand canonical catastrophe, and that ideal Bose gas stability turns on trap shape and dimension. He also defends symmetry-broken averages and rejects anomalous fluctuations in stable equilibrium. He writes for readers tripped up by the older literature.
arxiv-2604-03062: Li and Yang give a 2026 example of a smooth fourfold in positive characteristic whose Hodge-Witt numbers are asymmetric in total degree three. The example is sharp in both dimension and degree, and it comes from computing and approximating Hodge-Witt cohomology of the classifying stack of alpha-p. It shows the asymmetry can already appear at this low dimension and degree.
arxiv-2604-03962: Pride Kavumba and colleagues built StreamGuard, a streaming guardrail that forecasts harm instead of hunting for the first unsafe token. Prompt moderation sees full text, but streaming moderation must judge partial outputs, so StreamGuard predicts the expected harm of likely continuations from Monte Carlo rollouts. That allows early action without exact boundary labels. At the 8B scale it beat Qwen3Guard-Stream on input and streaming F1, reaching 97.5 F1 on a response-location benchmark.
arxiv-2604-04162: João Fontinha, Jorge Buescu, and Jaouen Ramalho studied how measures change for bilateral Laplace transforms of meromorphic functions on strips. With no poles on the split line, the values for two adjacent strips coincide. They derived explicit change rules for finitely many poles and conditions extending them to infinitely many poles. Uses cover analytic continuation of the zeta function, periodic functions, and Gamma quotients. A built entire function with distinct left and right representations yields a ghost transition, breaking uniqueness for the heat equation's Cauchy problem.
arxiv-2604-04362: Fontes and colleagues test how neodymium atomic data shapes kilonova light curves. Using SuperNu radiative transfer, they simulate a one-dimensional kilonova with a pure neodymium atmosphere. Transfer stays fixed while data comes from three codes: LANL, HULLAC and Autostructure. Data choice shapes light curves and spectra, with peak luminosities differing by nearly 1.5 between HULLAC/Autostructure and LANL sets. Near- to mid-infrared differences trace to neutral Nd I data, and a NIST-calibrated LANL set shifts late-time infrared structure, showing one lanthanide's data can reshape observables.
arxiv-2604-04462: Huang's thesis builds a framework for extracting thermodynamic work from quantum temporal correlations. An agent without quantum memory extracts work adaptively through inference under doubt. With rho-star plans, memory effects let adaptive plans beat fixed bounds. The work puts this in Time-Ordered Free Energy, an upper bound on adaptive steps revealing a thermodynamic gap tied to ordered discord. It tackles work extraction from unknown sources with reward learning. Adapting multi-armed bandit methods, an agent learns a quantum state and extracts work, with slow-growing waste beating tomography.
arxiv-2604-04562: Du and colleagues ran the open-source Paper Espresso for more than 35 months, processing over 13,300 trending arXiv papers and releasing all structured records publicly. The tool finds, summarizes, and studies preprints, with large language models writing structured summaries tagged by topical labels and keywords. The same models consolidate topics for daily, weekly, and monthly trend readings. Among the findings, reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning surged in mid-2025, and the most novel papers drew 2.0x median upvotes.
arxiv-2604-04962: Vivek, de Diego, and Banavar build structure-preserving integrators for nonholonomic mechanical systems on Lie groups. Retraction maps generalize the exponential map and give a handy tool for manifold integration. Since nonholonomic constraints restrict motion to a nonintegrable constraint set rather than the full tangent bundle, the authors use the Hamel formulation to write motion equations in coordinates matched to that set. On Lie groups, where dynamics and constraints share symmetries, the scheme simplifies. The integrator respects those constraints and their structure.
arxiv-2604-05162: Le and four colleagues present a system that controls mirrors without channel guessing. Smart radio panels promise rooms, yet rollout is choked by channel guessing cost. The system maps moving constraints to a virtual focal point space and uses central training, split runs. With MAPPO, agents learn team beam-aiming plans from user spots, giving CSI-free work. Tests show up to a 26.86 dB gain over static flat mirrors, with stable signal even under 1.0-meter position errors.
arxiv-2604-05362: Arora and Mahanta ask whether the matter-antimatter imbalance of the universe could come from decaying triplet fermions, heavy particles tied to neutrino mass, at energies experiments might one day reach. In the standard early-universe story those triplets must be enormously heavy to work. The team studies two non-standard histories instead: speedier early expansion, and a gravity theory built on a scalar field plus a tensor field. Faster expansion lets triplets of just a few teraelectronvolts succeed, while the gravity variant needs a few hundred teraelectronvolts.
arxiv-2604-05762: Hari Govind and six colleagues compute pion valence quark distributions in the light-cone quark model, evolving them to higher scales with DGLAP equations. Evolved distributions match experimental and theoretical extractions, and a first next-to-leading-order F2 prediction agrees with ZEUS and H1 data. Forward Drell-Yan cross sections and electron-ion collider kinematics extend the study.
arxiv-2604-06562: Lin and four colleagues test whether induced feelings sway small language models acting as decision makers. They steer model activations with crowd-checked emotion-laden texts, then run the models through cooperative and competitive game templates drawn from Diplomacy, StarCraft II, and everyday personas. Feelings shifted choices systematically, yet behavior stayed unstable and often diverged from human expectations, so the paper sketches ways to harden such agents against emotional disturbance.
arxiv-2604-06662: Zhu, Wang, and Gao harden image watermarks against removal and forgery attacks. Text-to-image diffusion watermarks already detect well, but adversaries can strip them or fake them. Their ISTS paradigm, instance-specific watermarking with two-sided detection, times injections and picks patterns from each user's prompt meaning. A new two-sided detector then strengthens detection robustness, and experiments show the design beats rival watermarks under both attack types.
arxiv-2604-06862: Wang and three colleagues test whether gas warps can induce galactic phase spirals. Phase-space spirals near the Sun, found in Gaia's second data release, are usually blamed on other bending-wave sources, while irregular gas inflow along the warp was neglected. Two N-body plus SPH simulations of an isolated galaxy hunt for warp-induced spirals with Fourier decomposition. Strong one-armed spirals appear in the warped run, persist about 10 Gyr, and track gas inflow and bending-wave amplitude, while the unwarped control shows only weak scattered spirals.
arxiv-2604-07262: Cutrupi and six colleagues give a direct way to tell excitons from free carriers in thin layered perovskites. They use light emission that varies with pump power, read through the Saha equation, to find the free-carrier share. The old power-law shortcut fails when the exponent sits between the pure exciton and pure free-carrier limits. Their tests on Ruddlesden-Popper layers match prior binding energies, map variation near grain edges at micrometer scale, and warn that strong pumping can skew readings under solar light.
arxiv-2604-07362: Pasandideh and Rettberg build an offline-online framework for safety-testing lane-following vision systems on edge devices. Heavy work happens offline: language models draft structured fault scenarios, and latent diffusion models synthesize sensor degradations, distilled into a lookup table for real-time use. A ResNet18 lane follower tested across 460 fault cases scores about 0.85 R-squared on clean data but degrades sharply under faults. Under fog, error rises by up to 99 percent and within-0.10 localization accuracy falls to 31.0 percent, exposing the limits of clean-data evaluation.
arxiv-2604-07562: Islam offers a reasoned system for cleaning label-free text clusters. Large language models act as meaning judges, not vector makers. Three stages follow: coherence verification, redundancy adjudication, and label grounding. Fit checks notes against member texts; it merges or rejects clusters by overlap. Labels come from a two-stage process making and merging similar labels without gold labels. Tests on two social media corpora show gains in fit and labels over rivals.
arxiv-2604-07962: Triantafillou and five colleagues argue that the term machine unlearning has been overloaded to cover two distinct problems. As models grow larger and train on more data, deleting specific points or behaviors after training draws intense interest. Different research efforts span two separate problem framings, yet the literature has not noted the distinction. That blur creates doubt about when an algorithm should work, poor metrics and baselines for comparisons, trouble interpreting results, and missed research directions. The note separates the two framings and maps the confusion they cause.
arxiv-2604-08062: Danry and four colleagues build a gaze-grounded multimodal assistant that reads users' cognitive needs from eye motion. Current language-model helpers answer well but lack action context showing when a user struggles. It uses first-person video with gaze layers to spot likely hard points and target follow-up help. A study with 36 participants compares the gaze-aware version against a text-only version. The gaze-aware version rates as much more accurate and tailored in judging reading habits, lifts recall, and elicits fewer spoken words, for leaner chats.
arxiv-2604-08162: Arcones and five colleagues develop a Bayesian framework that handles uncertainty while finding tendon breakage in pre-stressed concrete members from fine distributed fiber-optic data. These sensors watch strain changes across the surface of pre-stressed concrete members when such failure occurs. The team builds a finite element model of a tendon-breakage test and tunes its parameters with odds against sensor readings. To capture model-form uncertainty, random jolts go straight into material parameters, giving joint guesses of real traits and that uncertainty in one probabilistic model.
arxiv-2604-08262: Beaufort, Muñoz-Thon, and Richardson study marked magnetic action rigidity. An exact magnetic system on a closed manifold consists of a metric and a 1-form encoding a magnetic field. The team considers a broadened marked length rigidity conjecture. Can the marked magnetic action spectrum pin down the metric and form, up to a natural obstruction, for systems with Anosov magnetic flow? They answer it for nearby systems with close metrics and 1-forms, and also for metrics sharing a conformal class.
arxiv-2604-08362: Chen and thirteen colleagues build OmniBehavior, the first benchmark for mimicking people that draws only on real behavior records across settings and over long spans. Earlier tests, they argue, watch single scenes with narrow moves or invented data, missing how real choices link across scenes over time. Leading language models still struggle to copy such behavior, and their simulated people drift toward an overactive average person, flattening real differences and rare habits.
arxiv-2604-08562: Trofimenko and five colleagues build neural models that judge text to speech quality the way experts do, replacing slow costly human listening tests. NeuralSBS, backed by HuBERT, scores 73.7 percent on side by side comparisons, while improved MOSNet variants and a Whisper plus BERT ensemble predict absolute quality scores with error well below the human inter rater baseline. Naive text fusion by cross attention, they find, hurts rather than helps.
arxiv-2604-08862: Kebande applies stringology based cryptanalysis to the EChaCha20 stream cipher, hunting structural patterns that standard statistical tests may miss. EChaCha20 expands ChaCha20 with a 6 by 6 state matrix and a modified quarter round function. Yet no systematic study had checked whether those changes introduce keystream patterns, rotational biases, or partial collisions. He uses adapted Knuth-Morris-Pratt and Boyer-Moore algorithms for word level pattern analysis at 32 bits on one million keystream datasets. The cipher looks strongly random at 16 bit and 32 bit levels. Minor 8 bit irregularities remain.
arxiv-2604-09262: Semrén and colleagues study the near-equilibrium Einstein-Boltzmann system with a simple collision term for relativistic gases with inner states. Based on a BGK-type collision term, the Boltzmann equation is first rewritten in tetrad form. Heat coefficients are then found to first order in the Chapman-Enskog series for general spacetimes. These results build a self-consistent set of first-order equations, equivalent to the Einstein-Boltzmann system, for even models with viscosity and heat flow.
arxiv-2604-09762: Mukhopadhyay and Iguaz Juan use high-energy neutrino telescopes, including IceCube and ANTARES, to constrain primordial black holes as dark matter. For the first time, they derive limits on sub-asteroid-mass Schwarzschild black holes with extended mass functions. The limits come from the diffuse neutrino flux of direct evaporation and from transient signals of black holes passing near Earth. Their bounds run slightly weaker than gamma-ray limits but offer an independent probe from neutrino data. Future detectors such as IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT could improve these limits.
arxiv-2604-09862: Zhou and six co-authors present FF3R, a label-free feed-forward method joining shape and sense from multi-view images. Unlike earlier methods, FF3R needs no camera poses, depth maps, or labels, learning only from image training. A Token-wise Fusion Module adds to shape tokens with sense context, while Sense-Shape Mutual Boosting pairs shape-guided warping with sense-aware grids. Tests on ScanNet and DL3DV-10K lead in novel views, open-word cuts, and depth.
arxiv-2604-09962: Chen and Tseng construct a correspondence between genus 0 descendant Gromov-Witten theories of X and X prime for a simple flop X to X prime. They show the flop's Fourier-Mukai equivalence matches the descendant correspondence in a precise sense. The correspondence links the two theories' descendant invariants across the flop.
arxiv-2604-10062: Aguilar and six colleagues give an exact account of when attacks can work in linear MDPs under reward poisoning. Here, an attacker tweaks rewards within budgets to push a target agent to a preferred policy. Earlier work gave conditions for successful attacks, with little on when targeted attacks fail. Their theory separates vulnerable from robust cases, which resist attack without large costs even against plain non-robust learners. Treating deep learning settings as linear MDPs extends the theory, separating attackable from robust cases and attacking the vulnerable ones well.
arxiv-2604-10262: Ma and three colleagues pair a light-based reservoir computer with forward control for drone flight in tight spaces. Drones in tight, messy spaces suffer from nonlinear hidden motion like ground effects and wake swirl, missed by control. Their system uses laser light and optical feedback for built-in memory without history inputs, cutting training to ms and runs to ns. Tests show force guesses matching or beating CNN and MLP rivals while training only a linear readout. Feeding guesses into a PID loop lifts tracking balance.
arxiv-2604-10362: Hossain and three colleagues propose QPINN, a physics-aware network with quantum feature mapping for battery health outlook. Raw sensor data projects into a large Hilbert space, creating rich cues that capture subtle curved decay patterns, then a physics-aware network sets real constraints. The method reaches 99.46 percent average health scores across data sets, beating rivals, with error cuts up to 65 percent in MAPE and 62 percent in RMSE. Tested on 310,705 samples from 387 cells, it transfers between mixes without target health labels.
arxiv-2604-10462: Siqveland builds a Riemannian theory for varieties over associative algebras. First, he shows old varieties over closed fields can rest on any field at all. Local stand ins for simple modules then replace maximal ideal localization. Using smooth functions in place of polynomials lets differential tools run on these algebras. The payoff is a full frame with connections and geodesic curves.
arxiv-2604-10562: Buks tests a bold guess that quantum links can dissolve on their own. Spontaneous disentanglement tempts theory yet can break causality in some cases. To save causality, he rebuilds the guess on a maximum entropy footing. Lagrange multipliers then force the math to respect causal order. The rebuilt form fits any finite dimensional quantum system.
arxiv-2604-10762: Gabetti, Dolcini, and Girolami derive an efficiency bound for thermal engines that can beat Carnot's limit. The bound depends on statistical correlations between the engine's internal state and Hamiltonian, can saturate even in finite-time cycles, and covers classical and quantum engines alike. It gives the exact maximum efficiency for engines running with multiple baths, tightening Carnot's ceiling. A quantum-dot engine coupled to fermionic baths achieves the bound even beyond the quasistatic regime, offering a design principle for realistic energy-harvesting machines.
arxiv-2604-10962: Qiu and five colleagues propose ScoRe-Flow, a score-based reinforcement learning fine-tuning method for flow matching policies in robot control. It joins drift modulation with learned variance prediction, controlling mean and variance separately. Imitation-trained flow policies inherit demonstration limits, so beating weak behaviour needs reinforcement tuning. Noise-only control can hurt efficiency. Steering drift through the score function guides exploration toward high-probability regions, with a score from the velocity field. It converges more than twice as fast as prior art on locomotion tasks.
arxiv-2604-11062: Yan and four colleagues propose a capacity-region-achieving sparse regression coding framework over MIMO multiple-access channels. A single sparse code serves each user at transmission. With random semi-unitary dictionaries for encoding, multiple-access OAMP enables reliable parallel interference cancellation at the receiver. A coding principle with the multiple-access OAMP receiver achieves sum rate and, with time sharing, the entire region, guiding code design. Accordingly, the authors propose a coding scheme for such codes via power allocation over position-modulated signals.
arxiv-2604-11162: Lendering and two colleagues propose Boxes2Pixels for defect segmentation from noisy SAM masks. Defect segmentation matters for inspection, yet annotations are rarely available. But these labels are noisy, hallucinating background while missing defects. Boxes2Pixels treats SAM as a noisy teacher. Bounding boxes become masks offline by SAM. A student trains with a decoder over frozen DINOv2 features and correction relaxing background supervision when confident. On a wind turbine benchmark, anomaly mIoU rises by about seven points and binary IoU by about ten points. It uses 80 percent fewer parameters.
arxiv-2604-11462: Li and eight colleagues ease the context bottleneck for long-horizon language-model agents with active context curation. Their framework pairs a lightweight reinforcement-learned ContextCurator policy with a frozen TaskExecutor foundation model, decoupling context management from task execution. The curator prunes environmental noise while preserving reasoning anchors, sparse data points critical for future deductions. On WebArena it lifts Gemini-3.0-flash success from 36.4 to 41.2 percent while cutting tokens 8.8 percent, and on DeepSearch it reaches 57.1 percent against 53.9 percent with eightfold token savings. A 7B curator matches GPT-4o at context management.
arxiv-2604-11962: Walker, Humayun, Balestriero, and Baraniuk propose the Linear Centroids Hypothesis. It identifies network features with linear directions among centroid spaces, not middle-layer spaces. Each vector there denotes a centroid, or summary, of a local affine expert describing the learned input-output map. Swapping activations for centroids gives a drop-in alternative for standard analysis tools. The swap yields sparser, more useful dictionaries on DINO vision models, cuts spurious directions on a controlled task, finds clear circuits in GPT2-Large, and gives faithful saliency maps.
arxiv-2604-12162: Lu and 26 colleagues present AlphaEval, a benchmark of 94 agent tasks drawn from real work at seven companies across six job domains. Unlike tidy curated tests, real production work hides constraints, splits facts across documents, and calls for expertise no brief states, judged by standards that shift over time. AlphaEval tests whole agent products in several ways and adds a reusable pipeline for turning real requirements into runnable tasks.
arxiv-2604-12562: Massimo Villata offers a new explanation for two strange ANITA events from 2006 and 2014. The balloon observatory caught upward-going radio pulses over Antarctica. Ice reflections cannot explain them, and a cosmic ray from below the ice was ruled out. Villata turns to CPT gravity and its lattice Universe model. That model explains the pulses naturally, he argues, with no extra assumptions. It rests on general relativity plus matter-antimatter symmetry. Together with antihelium candidates from AMS-02, the events support a cosmos needing no dark energy.
arxiv-2604-12662: Mickaël De Backer and seven colleagues compare three hierarchical multi-component statistical methods. Patients' views matter at every stage of drug development. Generalized pairwise comparisons and desirability of outcome ranking lead the field. A newer Markov ordinal state transition model, MOST, lacks an explicit link to them. The paper compares all three through examples and structural analysis. Deep differences between the methods get full attention. The goal is guidance for teams choosing among them. The field keeps evolving.
arxiv-2604-12762: Myungchul Kim and three colleagues turn multi-camera person search into reasoning from witness dialogue and camera topology. Witness accounts are vague and partial. An agent plans, questions, and eliminates under information asymmetry. A Spatio-Temporal Topology Graph encodes camera links and transition times. The benchmark holds 2,691 tasks in 14 scenarios. Turn-Weighted Success scores correctness and efficiency. The best agent reaches 0.383 on track two and 0.590 on track three in tests. Removing tools drops accuracy by about 50 points, and removing reasoning halves success.
arxiv-2604-13162: Sharma, Srianand, Chand, and Guha measure how often a magnesium-II absorber seen along one quasar sightline also appears along a nearby sightline. Their sample holds 9,204 absorber pairs from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. Coincidence climbs steeply to about 5 to 8 percent below 100 kiloparsecs, then falls to a plateau near 1 to 2 percent out to 1 megaparsec. A single-halo model explains the small-scale boost while galaxy clustering explains the plateau, and stacked spectra imply a coherence scale near 100 to 200 kiloparsecs for cool metal-enriched circumgalactic gas.
arxiv-2604-13262: Maganti recasts medical image segmentation uncertainty as a decision problem, not just an output score. He casts segmentation as estimation followed by decision, showing that tuning uncertainty alone misses most safety gains on offer. Testing retinal vessel benchmarks with two uncertainty sources and three deferral plans, his confidence-aware deferral rule removes up to 80 percent of segmentation errors at only 25 percent pixel deferral. Cross-dataset toughness stays strong. Tuning gains, he finds, do not improve decision quality.
arxiv-2604-13462: Kapel and four colleagues build an incident-risk score for IT change at a large bank. Many IT incidents stem from changes, so the team predicts which changes risk incidents before deployment, aiding planning. To meet rules for auditability and explainability, they use SHAP values for feature insight. On a one-year real-world dataset, LightGBM beats the rule-based process and two rival models, especially with team metrics capturing organisational context.
arxiv-2604-13662: Samaha and six colleagues automate charge tuning for silicon quantum dots on 300-millimeter wafers, a bottleneck for scaling spin qubits. Their segmentation pipeline locates transition lines in full charge stability diagrams and returns gate voltages for the single-charge regime. Trained on 1,015 hand-annotated experimental diagrams across nine geometries and several fabrication runs, the model succeeds offline in 80 percent of cases, exceeding 88 percent for some designs.
arxiv-2604-13762: Liu, Yang, and Bu simulate winds in hot flows feeding a black hole, just inside the Bondi radius, and ask how radiative cooling changes them. As the accretion rate rises, cooling strengthens and thins the disk. Within the disk, the convectively stable region covers roughly 55 to 62 percent, so flows sit marginally stable. With weak cooling, winds drive the inward drop in inflow rate. With strong cooling, wind outflow falls sharply, and turbulence from magnetorotational instability and convection takes over the inward decrease.
arxiv-2604-13962: Kouloumvakos and colleagues investigate 26 solar energetic particle events with inverse velocity arrival, where high-energy particles arrive after mid-energy ones. Using Solar Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe data from 2018 to 2025, they rebuild each shock front in three dimensions. Connectivity starts on weak shock flanks and drifts toward the stronger apex, delaying high-energy arrivals and hardening spectra, with transition energy tracking shock speed.
arxiv-2604-14662: Liu studies how large a set looks when projected onto a curved family of hyperplanes in n-dimensional space. Take an analytic set of dimension at most n minus 2, projected along tangent directions of a curved surface. Liu proves the exceptional directions, where the projected dimension drops below any given level, form a set no larger than that level. Almost every direction therefore preserves the full dimension. In three dimensions with small sets, the estimate sharpens an earlier result by Gan and coauthors.
arxiv-2604-15462: Gkeneralis studies topological rigidity of real moment-angle manifolds built from flag simplicial complexes. Seeing the universal cover as the Davis complex, he shows it carries a CAT(0) metric, which forces its fundamental group to satisfy the Farrell-Jones conjecture. Surgery then gives the Borel Conjecture for these manifolds in dimension five and above, a stiffness that fails for complex and quaternionic twins.
arxiv-2604-15562: Guillemot and Voight deliver a full workflow that works out Belyi map monodromy exactly from equations over number fields via certified homotopy continuation. Run at scale, it verifies monodromy triples for Belyi maps in the L-functions and Modular Forms Database. The checked pipeline turns a fiddly computation into a result with proof behind it.
arxiv-2604-15862: Yijia Guo and 11 colleagues present Splats in Splats++, a method for hiding data inside 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, the 3D models built from splats, without breaking how they render. It grades spherical harmonics coefficients by importance for encryption, and adds a hash-grid opacity mapping plus a gated consistency loss to bind hidden and visible scenes tightly. Tests report up to 6.28 db higher message fidelity and 3 times faster rendering than prior methods, with strong resistance to structural attacks. The same approach also extends to 2D images and 4D dynamic scenes.
arxiv-2604-16062: Sun and three colleagues study reliable decoding for variable-length stop-feedback codes over correlated noncoherent fading channels. The decoding rule tracks information density for each channel realization. Since channel memory makes evaluation intractable, they derive usable finite-blocklength bounds on information density that hold over time along each sequence. The lower bound supports stopping-time analysis for VLSF decoding, while the upper bound references a characterized relaxation gap. A Gauss-Markov fading channel with Gaussian signaling illustrates stopping-time distribution and fading correlation effects.
arxiv-2604-16162: Horsman, Stepney, Clarke, and Kendon ask when a control system counts as computing, using abstraction and representation theory to test the question. They argue the plant being controlled acts as the user the theory requires, making computation possible in the system. Four cases, a digital thermostat, an electro-mechanical thermostat, a mechanical governor, and a human-run heating loop, show the framework at work across digital, mechanical, and open-loop designs.
arxiv-2604-16262: Sumanathilaka, Micallef, Hough, and Jayasinghe present SwanNLP, an entry to SemEval-2026 Task 5 on judging how plausible a word sense feels in a short story. Language models often disambiguate well on benchmarks, yet narrative contexts remain underexplored. Their framework scores homonymous word senses with structured reasoning, testing fine-tuned small models and dynamic few-shot prompting for large models. Commercial large models with dynamic prompting come closest to human plausibility judgments.
arxiv-2604-16562: Peng and colleagues tackle label noise in gaze guessing, where rough labels hurt transfer. They offer the first full study of label noise effects on transfer. Their SeeTN builds a meaning map through example-based change. That change keeps shape structure between gaze features and steady labels. Checking link match splits noisy from clean samples. Link smoothing in the meaning space moves gaze information from clean to noisy samples. Tests show SeeTN cuts source-domain noise and improves cross-domain transfer without losing source scores.
arxiv-2604-17162: Sharma and five colleagues use 109 fast radio bursts with redshifts and dispersion data to probe feedback's imprint on matter clustering. Dispersion measures trace baryon density fluctuations without bias from density or temperature, letting the team measure feedback effects on the matter power spectrum and gas fractions in galaxy groups and clusters. Fast radio burst data cut posterior variance at scales around one per megaparsec by a factor of about 8, matching other baryon tracers while probing redshifts below about 0.3 in a complementary regime.
arxiv-2604-17262: Yousefjani and Al-Kuwari show that an encoded field's layout can lift Stark probes to rapid scaling. For a 1D Stark probe with a steep gradient, Fisher information grows fast with system size, at the pinning shift. The scaling holds for mid-spectrum states and linked many-body states, and holds under fair resource analysis because the setup gap closes only algebraically. In motion, product-state start and free drift retain a boost, without cooling or narrow tuning. A superconducting build uses tunable transmon qubits coupled to a sensing bus.
arxiv-2604-17662: Khatami, Brandt, and Zaidman study real-world GitHub Actions run records to grasp workflow faults and uptake. The study counts 258,300 workflow run records from 952 repos, plus a close analysis of 21 diverse repos on how leads and helpers handle workflow results. It spots three distinct failure response patterns, finds higher workflow usage level goes with lower failure rates, and reveals a config-use gap where config files mask off or unused workflows.
arxiv-2604-18462: Breard, Elijas Parra, and de' Michieli Vitturi show diffusivity in granular-fluid mixtures is not intrinsic but emerges from pore-pressure diffusion plus granular compaction. From two-phase mass balance for a soft gas pile, they derive excess pore pressure changes over time. At the thin-flow, small-pressure limit, this reduces to a coupled diffusion equation with a source set by pore share changes. Modal analysis splits drainage from compaction, and a unit-free source-to-diffusion ratio unifies values across nearly two orders of magnitude of bed height.
arxiv-2604-18662: Singh offers coherence-gated routing, unlike routers that steer photons by energy state, a projective call that kills coherence. Here the call rests on the qubit's coherence size, read from weak joint checks. A photon passes if its coherence score, drawn from the stochastic master equation, tops a set bar. Coherence certified at emission powers a quantum random number maker with Bloch-sphere-bounded min-entropy. Lowballing detector efficiency steadies the math and curbs overcertification. A purity finding spots a shape loophole turning purity shortfalls into overclaims about 40 times.
arxiv-2604-18762: Thomson and eight colleagues present version 3 of the Public Health and Environmental Surveillance Open Data Model, an open relational model for wastewater surveillance. Fragmented data systems, inconsistent metadata, and poor interoperability have limited wastewater surveillance since the COVID-19 pandemic. Version 3 adds tables for public health actions, links to external repositories such as GISAID and GenBank, and notes on analytical workflows. Adopted by the Public Health Agency of Canada and adapted in Europe, the model is now used in over 25 countries.
arxiv-2604-18862: Long and three colleagues introduce Mutualistic Neural Active Learning for identifying bug reports across GitHub projects. A neural language model learns across projects, coupled with active learning. The most informative human labeled reports, plus their pseudo labeled counterparts, update the model. Reports awaiting labels are made more readable, cutting readability effort by about 96 percent.
arxiv-2604-19262: Lin and colleagues present CulturALL, a benchmark for testing language models on grounded multilingual and multicultural tasks, where answers must fit real-world, context-rich situations rather than trivia. Built with expert annotators plus language-model help, it holds 2,610 samples in 14 languages from 51 regions across 16 topics. The best model tested scores 44.48 percent accuracy, which the authors read as leaving substantial room for improvement.
arxiv-2604-19362: Blandin and colleagues test a computer model of radio wave travel through the human head during vowel speech. The model is built from magnetic resonance images taken while saying a, i, and u. It is checked against wave measurements from two people whose head shapes were modeled. Simulations and measurements agree well in broad terms, confirming the approach, with similar wave patterns across people for the same vowels.
arxiv-2604-19462: Chen and colleagues improve the upper bound on pth-order oracle complexity for convex-concave minimax problems with Lipschitz continuous pth-order derivatives. The previous bound was speculated to be optimal, since the best first-order method generalizes naturally to attain it. The authors obtain their improved upper bound by applying Monteiro-Svaiter acceleration. They also establish a lower complexity bound, suggesting a gap still exists for order 2 and above.
arxiv-2604-19562: Navarro, Tholke, and de Fabritiis present a method for structure-guided molecular design with contrastive 3D protein-ligand learning. Structure-based drug search must capture 3D protein-ligand interactions while searching huge chemical spaces. They present an SE(3)-equivariant transformer coding ligand and pocket structures into a shared embedding space. That encoder reaches strong zero-shot virtual screening results. The codes then feed a multimodal Chemical Language Model making target molecules.
arxiv-2604-19762: Parisel analyzes grapheme sequences in the Voynich Manuscript, a script of uncertain origin that has defied linguistic analysis. He finds two complementary structural layers. Inside words, a character-level right-to-left optimization holds; at word boundaries, a left-to-right dependency holds. This split appears in none of its four comparison languages: English, French, Hebrew, and Arabic. He also tests two generator classes against a four-mark joint test, and neither reproduces all four signatures across its full tested range.
arxiv-2604-19962: Boxan, Larrivée-Hardy, and Pomerleau benchmark radar odometry under the high tilt dynamics of subarctic terrain, where flat-ground assumptions fail. Test runs swing up to 13 degrees in pitch and 4 degrees in roll between scans, with absolute pitch reaching 30 degrees. Their new radar-inertial method uses tilt-proximity submap search and a hard cap on vertical displacement. It leads on an urban baseline and beats the runner-up by 0.3 percent on a two-kilometer dynamic route, with further tests on a high-slip ditch crossing.
arxiv-2604-20362: Gu derives spectral fluctuation-dissipation-response bounds for finite-state Markov jump processes. Matching causal susceptibility against its calm equilibrium standard, he bounds their mismatch across frequencies in terms of steady-state entropy production, probe variance, short-time perturbation spread, and reversible rest times. The bounds recover the standard fluctuation-dissipation theorem exactly at rest. They apply to causal susceptibilities you can measure, giving testable thermodynamic limits on theorem breakdown in driven steady states.
arxiv-2604-20462: Mughal and two colleagues release the largest cross-organization corpus of behaviour-driven development steps, from 347 GitHub repositories, plus a detector for duplicate Gherkin steps. The corpus holds over a million steps, and the detector layers exact hashing, normalized Levenshtein distance, sentence-transformer cosine similarity, and a hybrid of the last two. Calibration uses 1,020 hand-labelled pairs under a released rubric. The exact-duplicate rate weighted by step is 80.2 percent, with nearly nine hundred thousand eliminable step occurrences across the corpus.
arxiv-2604-20562: Sukhorebska gives the full list of equidistant decompositions of two spaces: the two-dimensional Euclidean plane and the two-dimensional sphere. The title frames the work as submetries onto one-dimensional space, and such a decomposition partitions a space into sets kept at equal distances from one another. The list covers both spaces fully, with no case left out.
arxiv-2604-20962: Bitonti, Hogan, and Mackay settle a conjecture of Feige and Pauzner about graphs where every vertex sits in both a large clique and a large independent set. They prove the conjectured exact value for the equal-size case. They also establish the optimal lower bound when the two sizes differ. The team extends the problem to edge-colored complete graphs. There, every vertex must sit in a monochromatic clique of each color, and they obtain upper and lower bounds.
arxiv-2604-21362: Linkai Liu and 11 colleagues tackle creative video generation for advertising, where text-to-video models struggle to match selling points to footage and to move realistically. Their knowledge-driven approach rests on an advertising creative knowledge base with two modules: semantic-aware retrieval linking selling points to videos, and multimodal knowledge reference supplying semantic and motion priors. Extensive tests show superior semantic alignment and motion adaptability over state-of-the-art rivals. Code and data will be open source.
arxiv-2604-21462: Michal Valko and four colleagues tackle conditional anomaly spotting, flagging data cases with odd outcomes or labels. Their approach uses the soft harmonic solution to estimate label confidence and spot anomalous mislabeling, tuned to avoid flagging lone cases or edge cases. Tests on synthetic and UCI sets show it beats baselines. A real-world electronic health record test seeks odd patient-management decisions, showing the method's practical reach.
arxiv-2604-21662: Ragnhild Laursen and colleagues sharpen mutational signature estimates by joining four add-ons to the usual setup: counting mutation chances, widening sequence context, using a negative binomial model, and setting signatures by formula. Mutational signatures track how often each base swap shows up with its near neighbors. The joined setup proves most useful when contexts span two or three neighbors on each side. Tests show the blend gives steady and trusted signatures in varied settings.
arxiv-2604-21862: Naskar and Manna realise epitaxial bismuth films on the magnetic insulator EuO(111) as a platform for topological states induced by proximity. Scanning tunneling microscope images show neatly ordered bi-layer bismuth in a quasi-square lattice, a stable alpha-phase bismuthene that is very flat. Tunneling spectra find a robust energy gap of about 400 milli-electron volts, matching a quantum spin Hall insulating phase lasting to room temperature, plus edge states at island boundaries. Cold magnetotransport on coupled ultrathin films shows linear magnetoresistance and a Hall sign reversal.
arxiv-2604-21962: Kavya, De, and Loo analyse perturbations and structure growth in Extended Proca-Nuevo gravity, a vector-tensor extension of General Relativity with a spin-1 field. The vector field changes expansion through a constraint, giving Hubble growth between Lambda-CDM limits, with shifts at middle redshifts. With minimal matter coupling, linear perturbation equations take a gauge-invariant form and growth of uneven patches is studied. This sector makes uneven stress and links a scalar mode to potentials, leaving the matter growth rule in General Relativity form but with changed history.
arxiv-2604-22162: Hirano and Ukita present SAMIDARE, a tracking-by-segmentation framework that strengthens SAM2MOT for crowded scenes. It adds density-aware mask re-generation and selective memory updates for adaptive mask control. State-aware association and new track starts add robustness under mutual occlusions and frequent frame-outs. On SportsMOT, SAMIDARE beats the baseline by more than 2 HOTA and 4.2 IDF1 points on the validation set. Adaptive mask control and state-aware association give a robust, efficient answer for dense sports tracking.
arxiv-2604-22362: Che and Perales introduce a timed-Gromov-Hausdorff distance for timed-metric spaces. They prove it is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the intrinsic timed-Hausdorff distance, thus inducing the same convergence notion. They prove a compactness theorem for that distance, from Gromov's compactness theorem. They then study causal structure and whether causality holds steady under timed-Hausdorff convergence. They also analyse causally-null timed-metric spaces and develop several basic traits. Finally, Gromov's compactness proof appears, from his paper on groups of polynomial growth.
arxiv-2604-22762: Patra and Vadgave argue product analytics should stop waiting for users to ask questions and start surfacing findings on its own. Their Behavioral Intelligence Platform turns raw event streams into accounts through four layers. First comes clean-up into a meaning ladder. Next a graph engine frames trips as end-state chains. Then a knowledge graph makes grounded facts, and spotting drives made insights.
arxiv-2604-22862: Srinivasan and Desikan test physics-informed neural networks, or PINNs, as solvers for two-flavor neutrino oscillation equations. The cases cover vacuum and constant-density matter, for reactor and atmospheric neutrinos. Ordinary solvers already handle these equations to machine precision cheaply, so the paper is a proof of concept. It benchmarks PINNs against NuFast and Runge-Kutta solutions. Network tuning yields high-precision agreement, setting a baseline for harder cases such as varying density profiles.
arxiv-2604-23362: Zhang and five colleagues introduce UniAda, a multi-objective white-box attack for autonomous driving systems that perturbs both steering and speed. Existing attacks focus on steering, missing speed controls and imperceptible perturbations. UniAda crafts an image-agnostic perturbation optimised jointly for steering and speed through an Adaptive Weighting Scheme. Tested on simulated and real driving data, it beats five benchmarks on two metrics. It induces steering deviations from 3.54 to 29 degrees and speed deviations from 11 to 22 km per hour on average.
arxiv-2604-23462: Bona-Landry extends a direct proof about the KPZ equation, which models randomly growing interfaces, from the open line to a finite interval with boundary conditions. Following an earlier argument based on Stein's equation, he shows that Brownian motion with constant drift stays invariant, up to height shifts, for the open equation. The result covers a general real drift parameter.
arxiv-2604-23562: Watanabe and colleagues show that simple eye measures can tell which side of the brain is at work. Pupil size and fixation length, tracked during one-sided tasks, sort left- versus right-side activity with a strong score. The result points to eye tracking for cognitive monitoring and rehab, and the team plans to extend the work toward live use.
arxiv-2604-23962: Ju simulates stirred, uniform turbulence to measure how long its energy cascade remembers its past. Intermittent bursts carry memory roughly three times the textbook length, while calmer stretches match that length, and the pattern flips near the smallest scales. Because the extra memory stays inside the middle range and ignores flow strength, the usual memory-free approximation for cascade equations looks far more restrictive than assumed.
arxiv-2604-24262: Moita and colleagues report MXT camera performance in flight aboard SVOM, which observes soft X-ray burst afterglows. Lobster-eye optics focus X-rays onto a camera covering a wide sky region around the ECLAIRs burst. Photon positions let onboard software localize sources rapidly, while spectra model burst properties on the ground. Early months in orbit tuned detector settings and calibration for availability and accurate spectra. The paper presents the ground-validated camera design, the in-flight tuning phase, and early mission performance.
arxiv-2604-24362: Binkowski tests whether hybrid quantum interior point methods can beat the HiGHS solver on realistic linear programming problems. Quantum methods promise polynomial speedups by handing Newton systems to quantum solvers, but speedups need not mean practical gains. Using a hybrid benchmarking approach with the best Chebyshev solver, he derives lower bounds on quantum runtime under generous assumptions. Across eight problem families, including MIPlib, quantum lower bounds exceed classical runtimes for any realistic cycle duration. The verdict is negative: these hybrid methods offer no practical advantage over classical solvers.
arxiv-2604-24462: Hume uses a Dvorak-Norin theorem to show that separation profiles and treewidth profiles of graphs grow at the same rate, settling a question raised by Huang, Hume, Kelly, and Lam. He then applies the equivalence to Cayley graphs built from tree-graded graphs, expressing their separation profiles through the profiles of their pieces. Such tree-graded graphs cover the Cayley graphs arising from free products of finitely generated groups.
arxiv-2604-24662: Martini, Abdelaleem, Gulati and Nemenman introduce DySIB, a method that learns low-dimensional state variables from high-dimensional time-series data without supervision. It keeps information that helps predict future windows from past windows, while penalizing representation complexity. It works entirely in latent space, without reconstructing observations. The test case is a pendulum on video, where the true state is known from physics. It recovers a two-dimensional representation matching the pendulum phase space. The learned two numbers track the swing angle and its speed, as they should.
arxiv-2604-24862: Butterworth and Spindler measure how image augmentations and dataset size affect a neural network trained to classify galaxy morphology. Astronomers often add augmentations assuming they always improve performance. Training versions of the Zoobot model on varied augmentations and dataset sizes from 230,000 Galaxy Zoo DECaLS images, they find augmentations improve performance. The gain shrinks as dataset size grows. The choice of sensible augmentations matters less than having augmentations. A saturation point exists where capacity is filled and augmentations cannot push past it. Simpler augmentations may suffice, saving time and resources.
arxiv-2604-24962: Lefterovici, Lelakowski and Perk test whether quantum breadth-first search can speed up maximum flow. Classically, Dinic's algorithm solves it with repeated breadth-first search and blocking flow steps. Quantum BFS replaces those steps with Grover's search, but test instances are too large for current hardware. So they run Dinic's algorithm classically, isolate BFS runtimes, and estimate gate counts for quantum BFS. Matching classical BFS would need gate times far below the physical record for most instances. For the smallest, most favourable instances, the gap is only about 1.3 times.
arxiv-2604-25062: Maddu, Chardès and Shelley build Probability Flow Matching, a way to learn random processes that match biology from single-cell data over time. They test it on three blood-formation data sets. Only the versions that respect biology get lineage changes, fate choices and gene-perturbation responses right. The method also copes with uneven populations, so cell growth and cell death can be learned at once.
arxiv-2604-25162: Angara and five colleagues present a sandbox platform for hybrid quantum-classical workflows in graph optimization. Quantum advantage, they argue, needs end-to-end case studies joining problem setup, quantum execution and classical refinement. Their workflow shrinks instances classically, optimizes with QAOA on IBM platforms and postprocesses to feasible solutions, avoiding direct constraint encoding. They study Minimum Vertex Cover, Maximum Independent Set and Maximum Clique on synthetic graphs, benchmarks and real networks. Hardware runs used a 156-qubit Heron r2 processor on graphs up to 128 vertices.
arxiv-2604-25862: Kogler and five colleagues present RESTestBench, a benchmark for language-model-generated REST API tests checked against natural-language needs. Coverage and crash scores poorly proxy whether tests check intended behavior. It pairs three services with verified requirements in precise and vague forms, plus a mutation metric for fault detection per need. Direct generation and refinement guided by the running system are tested across leading models. Success falls sharply when generators meet faulty code, especially for vague needs.
arxiv-2604-26062: Deng and seven colleagues design a learned data structure for a graph problem: tracking its strongly connected parts as directed edges arrive one by one, with all vertices known in advance. Their method takes a possibly faulty guess of the edge order and precomputes partial answers to speed up each insertion. With good guesses it hits nearly optimal bounds, and its speed falls gradually as guess error grows. Tests on real data sets confirm that the theory gains show up in practice.
arxiv-2604-26362: Kato and six colleagues ran computer models of liquid aluminum-titanium mixes with a machine-learning potential that transfers across settings, trained at first on solids. Against lab data, the liquid-state results agreed well, with excess volume and structural shifts caught faithfully. The runs told local packing apart from chemical ordering, which proved weak in this alloy. Flow resistance and diffusion were also tracked as heat and mix varied.
arxiv-2604-26462: Han and five colleagues built a multi-step pipeline for pulling set fields from long scanned bank documents in KYC checks. Such files run dozens of pages, are noisy and multilingual, and hide sparse key facts, so feeding them whole to vision-language models often fails. Their design splits page finding from deep reasoning, joining cleanup, multilingual OCR, mixed retrieval, and compact extraction. On 120 real-world documents, field accuracy rose by nearly 32 percentage points over whole-file baselines, with the best setup near 87 percent.
arxiv-2604-26562: Williamson and three colleagues derived rough formulas for two qubits sharing a bosonic reservoir in the mean-force Gibbs state. With no direct link, the qubits can still entangle through the shared reservoir, most strongly at the lowest temperatures. Entanglement shifts unevenly with coupling strength, and widening the reservoir spectrum beyond a single mode can strengthen it. The results map reservoir-mediated entanglement in thermal equilibrium and give a yardstick for number-crunching, framing strong coupling as a resource.
arxiv-2604-26662: Aalsma and Faruk study two-point correlations for heavy scalar fields in Nariai space. That geometry is a product of spheres with one sphere taken in complex form. Using the heat kernel method and a geodesic approximation, they obtain the correlator as a sum over complex geodesics, going beyond earlier results for pure de Sitter space. The phase of each geodesic share proves essential: accounting for it correctly avoids false blow-ups in the correlator that would otherwise appear.
arxiv-2604-26862: Ryan, Beckmann and Chandrasekhar use tunnel junctions to probe how quasiparticles move and relax in superconductors at millikelvin cold. Their three-lead copper and aluminum devices track quasiparticle charge and energy imbalance over spans near the coherence length. A dual-bias scheme splits out energy imbalance effects, and pair-breaking signals flip sign with bias voltage, with a sharp onset near three times the gap energy. Match with quasiclassical simulations gives the energy-dependent inelastic scatter time.
arxiv-2604-26962: Zhao and six colleagues present DeepTutor, an open-source agentic framework for tutoring that pairs citation-grounded problem help with level-matched question making. A hybrid personalization engine blends static knowledge grounding with dynamic learner memory, adapting each interaction to the student's changing needs. For evaluation they introduce TutorBench, an interactive benchmark with learner profiles drawn from university courses across five domains. It lifts personalized metrics by about 11 percent on average and strengthens general reasoning across five backbone models by about 29 percent.
arxiv-2604-27162: Flavin and Sen build a fast C++ engine for hide-and-seek games played by many agents under partial observability. Such Dec-POMDP settings are costly for reinforcement learning, which needs many samples. Their Hide-And-Seek-Engine uses data-oriented design, 64-byte cache-line alignment to cut false sharing, and a zero-copy bridge to PyTorch with pinned memory. The goal is cheap, high-throughput steps for human-AI joint operations.
arxiv-2604-27362: Li sharpens a deterministic algorithm for maximizing a monotone submodular function under a matroid constraint, focusing on its tuning parameter. He replaces a loose bound in the proof with the classical Pólya-Szegő inequality, which permits a smaller parameter choice and cuts the hidden constant in the query cost. A second, sharper tail bound for the logarithm matches the true expansion further and yields a near-best formula. The query class stays the same, and every inequality in the note is formalized and machine-checked in Lean 4.
arxiv-2604-27462: Liu and six others present IMPRESS, a tool that lifts graph few-shot learning, where models must adapt to tasks from only a few labeled nodes. Current methods learn node vectors in Euclidean space, which misses layered structure, and fit a target spread from few support samples even when it drifts. IMPRESS instead learns vectors in hyperbolic space, which suits layers, and grows the support spread through denoising diffusion. The authors prove a tighter general bound, and in tests IMPRESS beats rivals across benchmark data.
arxiv-2604-27562: Kveton and three colleagues propose a method for real-time learning with no explicit feedback, combining semi-supervised learning on graphs with online learning. The method builds a graphical picture of its world step by step, updating it from observed examples. Labeled examples supplied offline set the starting bias, while a stream of unlabeled examples gathered online refines it. The authors prove a regret bound on solution quality and test it on real-time face recognition, beating rivals on precision and recall across three video sets.
arxiv-2605-00162:
Argyro Sasli and 3 co-authors present EMBER, a software pipeline that hunts for a special kind of wave in the solar wind. These modulated ion acoustic waves can heat electrons as they pass. Experts have so far found them in Parker Solar Probe data by eye, a method that cannot cover the full mission archive.

EMBER turns short voltage bursts from the probe into sound-like spectrograms, then runs a suite of detectors that flag odd events without being told what heating looks like. The suite recovered most known events while keeping false alarms low. Flagged intervals also showed hotter core electrons than expected, matching the heating pattern found by earlier manual studies.
arxiv-2605-00262:
Deidre A. Hunter and Bruce G. Elmegreen look deep into ten nearby dwarf irregular galaxies, small systems with low stellar mass. Using ultra-deep optical images, they fit ellipses to the galaxies' faint outer light as a function of brightness. Far-ultraviolet images, which trace fresh star formation, serve as a comparison.

Large patchy regions of star formation, common even in the faint outer disks, skew the optical shapes of these galaxies. A few galaxies show hints of a separate stellar halo, but a stack of seven shows a smooth exponential falloff to very faint levels. The extended outer component is most likely disk, built by internal processes rather than material stolen from outside. Colors of the outer rings suggest ages of one to six billion years.
arxiv-2605-01062:
Suthakaran Ratnasingam offers a distribution-free procedure for detecting a single change point in a sequence of independent observations, using energy distance. Change points mark where a data generating process shifts, and finding them matters in genomics and beyond. Limit properties of the test statistic are derived under both the null hypothesis of no change and alternatives where a change occurs.

For a fixed split point the standardized score approaches a standard normal limit, while global detection uses the maximum over candidate splits with critical values from a permutation test. Simulations show much better robustness across error spreads than competing choices. Combined with binary splitting for multiple changes, the method is illustrated on breast cancer cell line genomic data from microarray measurements.
arxiv-2605-01362:
Ava Mohammadi, Rick Kramer, and Zoltan Nagy test how the control setup of a building district changes its work as a flexible load for the power grid. Districts must follow a target load curve while keeping people comfortable and sharing the control effort fairly.

They compare four setups on a 25-home district: central predictive control, solo learning agents, group-trained learning agents, and a hybrid that pairs district battery planning with per-home heating and cooling control. A rule-based controller sets the floor. Central control tracks well but leans on a few homes, causing more comfort breaches. Solo agents spread effort but drift off target. The hybrid wins overall, with the closest tracking, moderate comfort cost, and the most even spread of effort across homes.
arxiv-2605-01562:
Ahmed F Ibrahim rebuilds requirements reuse, the craft of adapting software specifications from old projects to new ones, as a guided walk over a formal model. The older framework he builds on matches names exactly and follows rigid templates, so it adapts poorly; language models adapt well but can emit invalid mixes of requirements.

His neuro-symbolic system pairs the two. A language model acts as a loose guide, proposing steps through a lattice of requirements from the older framework. A strict symbolic validator inside the loop blocks every structurally invalid combination. Hallucinated mixes are thus excluded by construction. On an autonomous benchmark over two application families, the system covers all requirements with a violation rate near zero. Its match to a single gold standard is only moderate, but every output is structurally sound and meets all mandatory domain rules, with audit trails for regulated settings.
arxiv-2605-01662:
Martin Q Ma and six co-authors answer long-video questions by choosing frames the way an active perceiver would: fetch what defies expectation. Uniform sampling of a long clip is costly and stalls in quality, so the frame budget needs aim.

Video Active Perception needs no training. A light text-conditioned video generator stands in for the model's prior knowledge of how scenes unfold. Frames that depart from that prior carry the news, and those are the frames the vision-language model is shown. Across five long-form and reasoning video sets, the method posts state-of-the-art zero-shot scores. It reaches them with far fewer frames per question than flagship baselines need, up to several times the frame efficiency. The picks also read as sensible to a human eye, landing on the moments the question is really about.
arxiv-2605-01762:
Hai-hong Li, Jun Song, and Feng-lan Shao read the recipe of two rare particles to learn the momentum spread of strange quarks just before they dress into hadrons. The ratio of the triple-strange omega baryon to the phi meson, tracked across transverse momentum, turns out to be governed by one feature: the curvature of that strange-quark spectrum.

Working in an equal-velocity combination model, where quarks moving together merge, the team extract the pre-hadron spectrum from measured phi data through a quark-number scaling step. They chart its curvature in proton and lead collisions at several LHC energies, in busy and quiet events alike. Feeding that curvature back through the model explains the observed momentum pattern of the ratio across all those systems. Strong collective flow built up in the partonic stage is discussed as the likely hand that bends the spectrum.
arxiv-2605-02062:
Jinhang Chai, Jianqing Fan, and Yihong Gu estimate a full conditional distribution with a neural generative method. Any such distribution can be produced by transforming a known noise variable, such as a uniform or normal draw, through a function of the inputs. The authors estimate that transform by minimising the energy distance between the true outcome distribution and the generated one.

Neural networks implement the estimator and can adapt to low-dimensional structure in the data on their own. The estimated distribution then serves tasks such as conditional moments, prediction intervals, and density estimation. Theory gives an oracle inequality with adaptive optimal rates for nonparametric problems. Simulations and a real data analysis show the method works in practice.
arxiv-2605-02162:
Arup Kumar Sarker and colleagues present AAFLOW, a runtime that makes agentic language model workflows scale in a reproducible way. Such workflows join retrieval, reasoning, and memory, but current frameworks scatter data handling, add serialisation cost, and run non-deterministically. They also lack a formal execution model drawn from high-performance computing.

AAFLOW models a workflow as a set of operators and builds communication-efficient plans. Using Apache Arrow and Cylon, it gives a zero-copy data plane so preprocessing, embedding, and vector search pass data directly. Resource-determined scheduling and asynchronous batching cut coordination cost. Experiments report pipeline speed gains up to about four and a half times, with language model throughput held comparable.
arxiv-2605-02962:
Barbara Tarantino and three co-authors introduce ISAAC, a post-hoc audit that checks whether a drug-target prediction model reasons from real molecular traits or from spurious ones. Strong benchmark scores can hide a model that leans on the wrong features, and plain accuracy cannot tell the difference. Their audit probes a frozen model with matched interventions, some mechanistic and some spurious, and compares its structural sensitivity.

Three sequence-based prediction architectures are audited on a standard benchmark. Models with near-equal accuracy, within a few points, differed by about a quarter in reasoning score, a gap stable across training seeds, intervention seeds, and two perturbation styles. The authors argue such structural auditing should accompany standard metrics in scientific machine learning, above all where a model's reasons matter as much as its score.
arxiv-2605-03062:
Anthony Bosman, Christopher W. Davis, Taylor Martin, and Katherine Vance measure how many crossing changes it takes to make a link trivial under a deep equivalence from clasper theory. That equivalence, introduced by Habiro, is tied to finite type invariants, yet for single knots it says little about unknotting.

For links the linking number blocks the same result, so the team handles the zero linking number case. They prove any such link with n parts needs at most n squared changes, and give examples needing a number that grows just as fast. They also settle the exact count when linking numbers are nonzero.
arxiv-2605-03162:
Jose M. Torres-Lopez, Sudipta Kundu, Felipe H. da Jornada, Tony Heinz, and Allan H. MacDonald model excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors placed under a periodic electric potential. These layered materials are a promising base for engineering exciton states, and an applied pattern can reshape them through the quadratic Stark effect.

Keeping only center-of-mass and valley degrees of freedom, they find the potential can split optical valley energies by up to about ten millielectronvolts and give valley-selective spread. Both effects depend on the trap's rotational symmetry. A non-degenerate lowest band with linear spread could also aid exciton condensation and superfluidity.
arxiv-2605-03262:
Taha Bouhsine introduces the Yat kernel, a new reproducing kernel built by multiplying an inverse-multiquadric distance term with a biased squared inner product. Standard inverse-multiquadric sections fade at infinity, raising the question of whether directional response can persist without losing universal approximation.

Bouhsine proves the new space contains the old one and stays universal on compact domains, while its sections keep a quadratic directional trace far away. High-dimensional covariance limits separate the kernels sharply under Gaussian inputs. The construction is also tight: three Yat atoms rebuild one inverse-multiquadric section exactly, and three are necessary.
arxiv-2605-03962:
S. M. Mehedi Zaman, Joao Couto, and Kiran Garimella map Americans' long-term information exposure on Facebook using a decade-long dataset of the public pages and groups followed by over eleven hundred users. That design lets them study potential exposure across hundreds of millions of posts from 2012 to 2023, addressing a gap in evidence about the platform's civic impact.

Political content made up a modest eighteen percent of the potential information diet, which was dominated by lifestyle and entertainment. Beneath that average sit persistent disparities: the volume and ideological leaning of political content differ sharply across age, gender, and racial lines, and political discourse frequently permeates nominally non-political spaces. Meta's 2018 Meaningful Social Interactions update is also assessed for its effect on these patterns.
arxiv-2605-04262:
Anju Rani, Daniel Ortiz-Arroyo, and Petar Durdevic present a public image data set for judging how much useful life is left in synthetic fibre ropes. Such ropes are used in offshore cranes, wind turbine work, and heavy lifting, where a failure can be dangerous and costly.

The set holds about thirty-four thousand high-resolution images of eleven rope samples worn out on a bend test machine under seven load levels. Ropes were loaded until they broke, and photos were taken at set intervals along their length, so users can track surface damage from new rope to failure.
arxiv-2605-04362: Samuel Everett proves a persistence result for periodic billiard orbits in polygons. In this setting, a ball bouncing inside a polygonal table follows a path that eventually repeats. Suppose a polygon has such an orbit, meeting a stated combinatorial condition. Everett then shows there are whole paths of polygons through the parameter space. Every polygon along those paths keeps a periodic billiard orbit of the same type. The result says these repeating paths are not fragile accidents of one exact shape, but can survive as the table is deformed.
arxiv-2605-04462:
Liening Qiao and three co-authors prove a stability result for a compressible magnetic fluid. A uniform state stays stable against small disturbances. Their idealised plasma model has velocity damping, but no viscosity or electrical resistance. Global results of this kind had been missing for the multi-dimensional version of these equations.

Working on a periodic box, they assume two things. The starting disturbance is small enough in a strong smoothness measure. The background field also satisfies a number-theoretic condition. They then show a unique smooth solution exists for all time. It decays at an algebraic rate. The proof uncovers a hidden dissipation created by the coupling between velocity and magnetic field.
arxiv-2605-04562:
Peiyue Ma and nineteen co-authors study how oxygen content controls superconductivity in a layered nickel oxide that belongs to a family drawing intense interest for high-temperature superconductivity. Making clean samples is hard because oxygen levels vary and different layered phases grow into each other.

By tuning oxygen precisely, the team produced samples ranging from a pure bilayer phase to mixtures with hybrid and trilayer intergrowths, verified by structural and compositional analysis. High-pressure electrical measurements show distinct superconducting transitions tied to each phase. Oxygen content thus governs both phase purity and the superconducting behaviour itself, giving makers a concrete handle for improving these materials.
arxiv-2605-04762:
Yiming Wang and three co-authors introduce a benchmark for two-way generation between T-cell receptors and the peptides they recognise. That pairing sits at the heart of adaptive immunity. It also drives personal immunotherapy and vaccine design. Modelling that match is hard. Data are scarce, sequence links are complex, and no standard evaluation existed.

Their benchmark defines both directions as sequence generation tasks, supported by a curated data set of tens of thousands of checked receptor-peptide pairs with no MHC restriction confound. Evaluation mixes speed, sequence accuracy, and biological sense. Testing recurrent, convolutional, and transformer models reveals the key trade-offs among current architectures.
arxiv-2605-05162:
Cătălin Paşcu Moca and three co-authors study how spin correlations evolve in a one-dimensional XXZ spin chain that also loses and gains spins through contact with a reservoir. Starting from a plain mixed steady state with some magnetisation, the time-dependent correlations on top of it turn out rich. Without the reservoir, the along-chain correlators reproduce the known transport classes, from ballistic to diffusive.

Extra ballistic light-cone spreading appears at finite magnetisation, traced to magnon motion, while the transverse correlator behaves very differently across regimes. With full reservoir dynamics included, the early-time universality classes survive, but correlations gain an overall exponential fading at long times. Simulations and exact results support the picture.
arxiv-2605-05262:
Yuelin Hu and four co-authors ask how to spend a fixed rollout budget wisely when training tool-using agents with group-based reinforcement learning. Many sampled attempts end with uniform outcomes, which inject no useful gradient signal. The authors formalise rollout informativeness as the expected surviving gradient mass and prove that budget-blind independent sampling keeps a stubborn collapse rate on hard prompts.

Recasting state selection as a submodular maximisation problem gives a greedy selector with a classic approximation guarantee, and their confidence-bound terms fall out of that objective in closed form. Their InfoTree framework adds a learned budget allocator and speculative expansion, raising mixed-outcome ratios while cutting overhead in tests across nine benchmarks.
arxiv-2605-05362:
Sheng Long and five co-authors test whether future space-based gravitational wave observations of extreme mass-ratio inspirals can measure a Lorentz-symmetry-breaking parameter in bumblebee gravity. Such inspirals, a small object circling a huge black hole for many orbits, probe strong-field geometry and test general relativity precisely. The authors build waveforms for a Schwarzschild-like black hole in this modified gravity theory.

The breaking parameter changes orbital evolution and hence the waveform, with effects growing for larger values and more eccentric orbits. A Bayesian analysis recovers all injected source parameters within their uncertainty intervals. The parameter itself could be constrained to an uncertainty around one part in ten thousand by the future LISA observatory, they find.
arxiv-2605-05462:
Hope Duncan writes on the modal logic of symmetric extensions, a construction from set theory. Symmetric extensions generalize the forcing method and produce a multiverse of models, some with the axiom of choice and some without. Modal logic, the logic of necessity and possibility, can describe the structure of that multiverse.

Duncan defines a notion called choice-switches inside this setting. The note shows that any independent system of choice-switches is not itself independent from any standard example of an independent system of buttons. The result links two basic devices used to reason about the set-theoretic multiverse.
arxiv-2605-05562:
Survey-based AI forecasts need error bars that hold for every subgroup, not just on average. Amir Rafe and Subasish Das study conformal prediction for five-level AI-attitude forecasts in a large Pew survey panel. They compare standard split conformal methods with group-specific Mondrian versions across one hundred splits.

Standard methods hit their average coverage targets but left subgroup gaps near thirteen points. Group-specific calibration made the strongest model's trade-off worse, not better. A regularized version that shrinks group thresholds toward the global one softened the problem without a clear fairness win. Marginal validity, they conclude, is not enough.
arxiv-2605-05662:
Safety tests for language models are mostly written in English and translated, missing harms that only make sense in one country. Dasol Choi and sixteen co-authors build XL-SafetyBench, a benchmark grounded in ten country-language pairs. It contains 5,500 test cases in two suites: jailbreak prompts rooted in local contexts, and cultural probes hiding sensitivities inside innocent-looking requests.

Each item passed automated validation and two independent native-speaker annotators. The design separates principled refusal from mere comprehension failure. That distinction lets evaluators tell whether a model understood a local taboo and still answered badly.
arxiv-2605-05862:
Neural operators learn mappings between functions and shine on regular grids, yet they stumble on irregular domains. Yanming Xia and Angelica I. Aviles-Rivero argue the failure deepens layer by layer. Because each layer mixes information globally, the network progressively loses access to the domain's geometry, a failure they formalize as the geometric forgetting hypothesis.

Layer-wise probes confirm that both spectral and attention-based operators shed geometric fidelity with depth. Accuracy, stability, and generalization suffer accordingly. The authors introduce a lightweight remedy that re-injects geometric information, turning a diagnosed failure mode into a design principle for operator learning on complex domains.
arxiv-2605-06262:
Robert Ganian and Marlene Gründel introduce bilateral treewidth, a new measure for making quantified Boolean formula checking tractable. Treewidth captures how tree like a formula's structure is, and satisfiability is easy at low treewidth. Quantified formulas stay hard even then, since plain treewidth ignores which variables are existential or universal and the order they are quantified in, the authors explain.
